mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% in the month preceding the prediction window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average of the same period in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns outperform the 60-day moving average of the prior 12 months by at least 1 standard deviation (z-score > 1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in PAYEMS accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE signals a strengthening labor market that raises wage growth expectations, which in turn supports higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in at least 60% of similar monthly labor market events (rolling window of 24 months).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 of at least 3% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level indicates a cyclical contraction in business fixed investment, which lowers growth prospects and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive months by ≥ 3% then rebounds in the third month
regime_hint: Early stage of business investment cycle contraction
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in INDPRO above 1.5% suggests accelerating supply-side expansion, which, when combined with falling UNRATE, reduces the cost of capital and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 1.5% in the month preceding prediction while UNRATE < 6.5%
regime_hint: Supply-side expansion with labor market moderation
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior 3-day average (z < 1.65).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period where FEDFUNDS remains below 1.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower borrowing costs and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 20-day average of the previous 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in HOUST accompanied by a decline in PAYEMS below the prior month's level suggests weakening demand for consumer goods, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by > 10% month-over-month while PAYEMS falls by > 2% in the same month
regime_hint: Demand softening in consumer discretionary sector
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in at least 80% of similar monthly events (rolling window of 24 months).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month while INDPRO remains flat, it signals a sudden contraction in inventory investment, raising uncertainty and predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by > 10% in a month and INDPRO does not change direction
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average of the prior 12 months (z < -1.65).
